cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: There are 10 components of fitness that you need to know for GCSE PE. They are divided into health-related and skill-related components.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The ability of the heart, lungs and blood vessels to deliver oxygen to working muscles over a prolonged period of time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The ability of a muscle or group of muscles to sustain repeated contractions, or to continue applying force against a fixed object, over a period of time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The range of movement possible at a joint.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The maximum force a muscle or group of muscles can exert in a single maximal contraction.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The ability to exert a maximal force in the shortest possible time. It is a combination of strength and speed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The maximum rate at which an individual can cover a distance or perform a movement.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The ability to change direction quickly and precisely while maintaining balance and control.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The ability to maintain the body's centre of mass above the base of support, whether stationary (static balance) or moving (dynamic balance).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The ability to use two or more body parts together smoothly and efficiently.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Components of Fitness
cards.back: The time taken to initiate a response to a stimulus. It is the gap between the presentation of a stimulus and the start of the movement.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — components of fitness?
cards.back: 1. For Components of Fitness questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Components of Fitness to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
